The four data inputs on the left are labeled P, Q, R, S from top to bottom, and inside the multiplexer they correspond to numbers 0, 1, 2, 3. The output on the right is labeled F(X,Y). There are two select lines at the bottom, indicating that S1 is MSB and S0 is LSB; in the figure X is connected to S1, and Y is connected to S0, so the select value XY=S1S0. The side note states S1 and S0 are the select lines. Then reason: In a 4:1 MUX, when the select lines S1S0=00, input 0 is selected, namely P; when 01, input 1 is selected, namely Q; when 10, input 2 is selected, namely R; when 11, input 3 is selected, namely S. Construct a truth table for F(X,Y)=X\bar{Y}+\bar{X}: when XY=00, X=0, so \bar{X}=1, F=1; when XY=01, X=0, so \bar{X}=1, F=1; when XY=10, X=1 and \bar{Y}=1, so X\bar{Y}=1, F=1; when XY=11, X=1, Y=1, so X\bar{Y}=0 and \bar{X}=0, F=0. Therefore P=1, Q=1, R=1, S=0.
